Liverpool Council approved $5000 for a photo wall of politicians, sparking backlash from residents and MPs who argue the funds should be used for road and park maintenance.

The Bright Side:
It creates a digital archive of local history that might otherwise be lost over time.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT error. They frame it as 'civic history' when the reality is 'self-promotion' at the expense of public service.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic case of power projection. By prioritizing a 'hall of fame' over potholes, the council signals that their own image is more important than the basic services they were elected to provide.

The Trajectory: The Path of Reckoning.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The cost of vanity is the erosion of public trust.

The Unavoidable Truth: The council has the funds for maintenance.

The Unavoidable Lie: The photo wall is a necessary civic expense.

Alethekanon:
This is a failure of institutional humility. When a council prioritizes a display of its own members over the physical safety and cleanliness of the streets, it reveals a disconnect from its primary mandate.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see leaders focus on their own portraits when families are struggling with dangerous roads. True service is found in the work, not the wall.

Brothekanon:
Five grand for a wall of selfies? You could fix a lot of potholes for that. Maybe they should put a picture of a pothole on the wall so they don't forget what they're supposed to be fixing.
